title: What AI governance demands of the teams putting it into practice
headline: Moving from AI governance principles to implementation
summary: Discussions at the IAPP Privacy. Security. Risk. + AI Governance conference in Seattle highlighted a shift toward practical implementation, focusing on risk assessment, accountability, auditability, and human oversight. Organizations must connect each AI use case to a responsible owner, define permissions for agentic systems, and maintain clear evidence supporting approval and auditability.
why_it_matters: Data leakage, model security and agents with excessive permissions make AI security a board-level issue that requires visibility into material exposures and evidence that management can detect and contain failures.

quotes.text: Along with optimism about AI’s productivity benefits, discussions focused on risk assessment, accountability, auditability and human oversight.
Data leakage, model security and agents with excessive permissions can affect customer trust and business continuity.

classification.significance_reason: Provides practical practitioner commentary on implementing AI governance, accountability, and vendor risk management, but introduces no new laws or binding standards.
